title: Altered cortical thickness following prenatal sodium valproate exposure.
ehr_evidence: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scans were acquired on the 3T Siemens Magnetom Trio at Murdoch Childrens Research Institute, Melbourne, using a 12-channel coil.
summary: A case-control neuroimaging study of 16 children prenatally exposed to sodium valproate and 16 matched controls found regionally increased cortical thickness and loss of normal inferior frontal asymmetry following in utero VPA exposure.
key_findings: Increased cortical thickness in the left inferior frontal gyrus (Pars Opercularis) and left medial occipital cortex (Pericalcarine), remaining significant after controlling for age.
A significant interaction between group and hemispheric inferior frontal thickness (F(1, 29) = 12.38, P = 0.001) showed absence of the normal right > left asymmetry in VPA-exposed children.
VPA dose across pregnancy correlated significantly with right IFG thickness (r = 0.57, P = 0.02) but not left IFG thickness (r = -0.17, P = 0.53).
A non-significant trend toward poorer verbal abilities and greater left IFG thickness (r = -0.42, P = 0.12).
Total cortical white and grey matter did not differ between groups (both P > 0.1).
captured_features: Cortical thickness (Freesurfer voxelwise group comparisons, P < 0.05 Monte Carlo correction)
Total cortical white and grey matter volume
population: 16 children (7 male, 1 left-handed) exposed to VPA in utero (mean age 7.2 years, range 6-8) and 16 age- and sex-matched controls (mean age 8.1 years, range 6-9) at Murdoch Childrens Research Institute, Melbourne, Australia.
exposure_domain: prenatal drug exposure (sodium valproate / antiepileptic drug)
limitations: Very small sample size (16 exposed vs 16 controls).
Minor but significant age discrepancy between groups.
Cohort exposed to a relatively low average VPA dose, limiting dose-response generalizability.
Cross-sectional design precludes causal inference about developmental trajectory.
